      18             "Superstorm Sandy" brought great devastation

       1      in recent years.

      18      Vice Chair Farley, Ranking Member O'Brien,

      19      Senator Marcellino.

      23      when I start, and introduce two people that are with

      24      me today:

      25             One is, Kate Powers, to my left, who is --





 

                                                                   7
       1      who runs our legislative shop;

       2             As well as, Dan Burstein, who you probably

       3      haven't met before.  He is our executive deputy

       4      superintendent for real estate for our real estate

       5      finance division.  He has led the charge on these

       6      issues for us.

      10             As you said, Mr. Chairman, the impact of

      11      "Storm Sandy" really can't be overstated.  The -- it

      12      brought incredible devastation over, really, a

      13      shocking geographic -- shockingly large geographic

      14      region, and it underscored the importance of

      15      insurance.

      16             This is not the Insurance Committee, but

      17      we're talking about an insurance issue today in many

      18      ways.

      19             This is what people have insurance for.  This

      20      is why people pay premiums, months after month

      21      after month, year after year, for when a catastrophe

      22      like this occurs.

      23             And right after the storm, Governor Cuomo was

      24      very clear with DFS and, frankly, with me

      25      personally, that we needed to take whatever steps





 

                                                                   8
       1      possible to maximize private-insurance payments,

       2      where appropriate under the existing contract, were

       3      getting to "Sandy" victims, and they were getting

       4      to "Sandy" victims quickly, so that there could be

       5      a more robust and effective rebuild.

       6             So that's what we've tried to do at DFS.

       7             We've worked very hard in the early days

       8      after the storm to get adjusters to individuals'

       9      homes and to get insurance money flowing.

      10             And that was difficult, initially, but as the

      11      insurance checks began to be cut to homeowners,

      12      we began a see a new problem, as you've outlined,

      13      Mr. Chairman.  Banks and mortgage servicers, who

      14      were required to co-endorse these insurance

      15      checks, were causing a bottleneck, and delaying

      16      the flow of funds, not intentionally, but that was

      17      what was developing.

      18             And as more insurance money began to flow,

      19      week after week after the storm, the holdup became

      20      worse and worse, and it was really very tough on

      21      homeowners.  It was a -- what we call a

      22      "double-whammy."

      23             They were homeowners who had run the gauntlet

      24      with their insurance companies, and, finally, gone

      25      through that whole process to get their insurance





 

                                                                   9
       1      money, and expected to now get it, were all of a

       2      sudden faced with a whole second round of red tape.

       3             They were often at this point, exhausted;

       4      their homes were ruined; it was cold; it was

       5      getting colder and colder outside; and they were

       6      having trouble getting their money.

       7             It was, you know, a real problem that we

       8      encountered at that point.

       1      that insurance money flow to the rebuild, and flow

       5      agreement with ten of the major banks and

       6      servicers that enabled homeowners to get their

       7      insurance advanced payments faster.

      11      begin their rebuild and their repairs.

      14      as the advanced payments were being depleted,

      15      final settlement checks were still getting

      16      bottlenecked at the banks.

      18      banks, to learn exactly how much "Sandy" insurance

      19      money was being held up there.

      21      February, that there were approximately

      22      6,600 checks that weren't out of the banks yet,

      23      valued at more than $208 million, with the four

      24      biggest banks accounting for about 130 million of

      25      the 208 million dollars.

       1             Given these findings, the department, at

       2      the Governor's direction, took a number of steps.

       7      documentation they were requiring, and to release

      14      country, that part of the problem was the guidance,

      22      Secretary of HUD, Sean Donovan; FHFA; and the

      23      GSEs.  There are now new guidelines that are just

      24      out, that will, for current borrowers,

      25      significantly speed up the flow of money.
